## LotConsumption

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ledger.LotConsumption</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ledger/LotConsumption.cs:11](../../../../src/Meridian.Ledger/LotConsumption.cs#L11).

Shared open-lot consumption walk used by every lot-accounting engine (ledger tax-lot relief, paper-trading positions, backtest portfolios, and metrics attribution). Walks lots in the caller-chosen relief order, taking min(remaining, lotQuantity) from each lot and splitting the final partial lot, until the requested quantity is consumed or lots run out. Callers own ordering, rounding, realized-P&amp;L formulas, and how a shortfall is handled (throw, clamp, or flip), so engine-specific accounting semantics stay at their call sites.

## PartnersCapitalStatementLayout

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ledger.PartnersCapitalStatementLayout</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ledger/PartnersCapitalStatementLayout.cs:55](../../../../src/Meridian.Ledger/PartnersCapitalStatementLayout.cs#L55).

A bespoke, client-grade layout of the statement of changes in partners&#x27; capital. Unlike the generic LedgerReportTable projection, this model keeps money typed, classifies each account by partner role, computes each partner&#x27;s ownership percentage of ending capital, and anchors the statement to the fund&#x27;s ledger-backed net asset value (the unitized NAV base) with an explicit reconciliation flag. It is a pure projection over a LedgerPartnersCapitalStatement — it introduces no new ledger fact.

```csharp
public sealed record PartnersCapitalStatementLayout(string FundId, string PeriodId, string BaseCurrency, DateTimeOffset PeriodStart, DateTimeOffset AsOf, decimal NetAssetValue, bool TiesToNetAssets, IReadOnlyList<PartnersCapitalStatementLine> Lines, PartnersCapitalStatementLine Total)
```

## PortfolioPricingRule

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ledger.PortfolioPricingRule</code>. Kind: `record`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ledger/PortfolioPricingRule.cs:10](../../../../src/Meridian.Ledger/PortfolioPricingRule.cs#L10).

A portfolio-scoped pricing rule that selects the price source, valuation method, and ASC 820 fair-value level to apply to a class of instruments in one portfolio, effective over a date window. This is the per-portfolio complement to the fund-scoped DailyPortfolioPricingPolicy: the policy states the fund&#x27;s default valuation posture, while an ordered set of these rules lets administrators override the source/method for specific instrument types within a portfolio.

## PostingCalculationNotYetConnectedAttribute

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Ledger.PostingCalculationNotYetConnectedAttribute</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Ledger/PostingCalculationNotYetConnectedAttribute.cs:11](../../../../src/Meridian.Ledger/PostingCalculationNotYetConnectedAttribute.cs#L11).

Declares that a posting calculation (a method that builds journal drafts or journal lines) is finished but deliberately has no production caller yet. The structural test PostingCalculationConnectionTests fails for any posting calculation that is neither called from production source nor carries this marker, so an unconnected calculation is always a recorded decision with a reason instead of an accident.

Computes a compounding (or simple) preferred return on an investor&#x27;s contributed-capital timeline using Actual/365 day-weighting. The pref accrues on outstanding contributed capital; in compound mode accrued pref capitalizes into the base at each cash-flow boundary.
